children.text: bhālaṃ vahniśikhāṅkitaṃ dadhad adhiśrotraṃ vahan saṃbhṛta
krīḍatkuṇḍalijṛmbhitaṃ jaladhijacchāyācchakaṇṭhacchaviḥ /
children.translated_text: sport of playful coiling serpents, with a throat-luster fair as the shadow of the ocean-born [moon],
Bearing a forehead marked by the crest of fire, wearing above the ear the

children.text: vakṣo bibhrad ahīnakañcukacitaṃ baddhāṅganārdhasya vo
bhāgaḥ puṃgavalakṣmaṇo 'stu yaśase vāmo 'tha vā dakṣiṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: that half bearing the mark of a mighty bull, be for your glory — whether the left or the right!
displaying a chest adorned with the armor of serpent-skins — may the half of the One whose other half is a woman,

children.text: vāme sāñjanam akṣi dakṣiṇadiśi śyāmāyamāno galaḥ
pāṇau tiṣṭhati darpaṇo 'tra mukuṭe 'mutra sthitaś candramāḥ /
children.translated_text: a mirror rests in one hand, while a crescent moon is set upon the other's diadem.
On the left, an eye adorned with collyrium; on the right side, a throat darkening to dusky blue;

children.text: tan māteyam ayaṃ piteti sucirāt sapratyabhijñaṃ śanair
yasyotsaṅgam agād guho bhavatu vaḥ prītyai sa gaurīśvaraḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Guha</s> (Skanda) climbed into the lap [of the composite form]. May that <s>Gaurīśvara</s> (Lord of <s>Gaurī</s>) be for your delight!
'That is Mother; this is Father!' — recognizing them after a long time, slowly, with dawning remembrance,

children.text: muñcebhājinam asya kumbhakuhare muktāḥ kucāgrocitāḥ
kiṃ bhālajvalanena kajjalam ataḥ kāryaṃ tavākṣṇoḥ kṛte /
children.translated_text: 'What need of fire on his brow? Collyrium should be applied for the sake of your eyes!'
'Remove this elephant-hide from the cavity of his [water-]pot! The pearls belong on the tips of her breasts!'

children.text: saṃdhāne vapurardhayor bhagavator itthaṃ niṣedhe 'py aheḥ
kartavye priyayottarānusaraṇodyukto haraḥ pātu vaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Hara</s> (Śiva), eager to follow the beloved's subsequent [instructions] about what must be done, may he protect you!
Thus, in the joining of the two body-halves of the Blessed Ones, even when the serpent [ornament] is being protested,

children.text: vihitam ajagośṛṅgāgrābhyāṃ dhanur ghaṭitaṃ tathā
narakaraṭinor dehārdhābhyāṃ gaṇaṃ parigṛhṇataḥ /
children.translated_text: formed from the two body-halves of a man and a female elephant, encompassing [his] retinue —
A bow fashioned from the tips of the horns of a wild goat, and likewise a body

children.text: dvividharacanāvāllabhyānāṃ nidher ucitā vibhor
jayati laṭabhāpuṃbhāgābhyāṃ śarīravinirmitiḥ //
children.translated_text: a treasure worthy of a collection of ornaments of two different designs!
victorious is the body-creation of the Lord, from the female and male halves,

children.text: nedaṃ parṇasamīraṇāśanatapomāhātmyam ukṣoragau
paśyaitāv ata eva saṃprati kṛtau tanmātravṛttī bahiḥ /
children.translated_text: behold, these two — the bull and the serpent — have been reduced to bodies sustained by mere subtle elements!'
'This is not the greatness of subsisting on leaves, wind, and fasting austerity;

children.text: premṇaivārdham idaṃ carācaraguroḥ prāpeyam ātmastutīr
itthaṃ devavadhūmukhāc chrutisukhāḥ śṛṇvaty aparṇāvatāt //
children.translated_text: delightful to hear, <s>Aparṇā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>) listens to from the mouths of the divine maidens.
'Through love alone I obtained this half of the Teacher of all moving and unmoving things!' — such self-praises,

children.text: kāpy eteṣu ruciḥ kaceṣu phaṇināṃ puṃskokilasyeva te
gobhiḥ kaṇṭhataṭasya hṛṣyati puro dṛk paśya cakṣuḥśruteḥ /
children.translated_text: 'your throat-slope thrills at the cows' [lowing]; look ahead — behold the wonder of hearing through the eyes!'
'What strange delight in these tresses among the serpents! Like a male cuckoo',

children.text: saṃdhāne 'bhinave mitho bhagavator jihvāpṛthakspandinī
bhinnārthāṃ sadṛśākṣarām api vadanty evaṃ giraṃ pātu vaḥ //
children.translated_text: yet uttering speech with identical syllables but different meanings — may that [speech] protect you!
At the novel junction of the two Blessed Ones, each tongue moving independently,

children.text: dātuṃ vāñchati dakṣiṇe 'pi nayane vāmaḥ karaḥ kajjalaṃ
bhaujaṅgaṃ ca bhuje 'ṅgadaṃ ghaṭayituṃ vāme 'pi vāmetaraḥ /
children.translated_text: and the right hand wishes to fasten a serpent-armlet on the left arm too.
The left hand wishes to apply collyrium to the right eye also,

children.text: itthaṃ svaṃ svam aśikṣitaṃ bhagavator ardhaṃ vapuḥ paśyatoḥ
sādhārasmitalāñchitaṃ diśatu vo vaktraṃ manovāñchitam //
children.translated_text: may their face, marked with a shared smile, grant you your heart's desire!
Thus, as the two halves of the Blessed Ones' body, each untrained in the other's ways, behold [each other],

children.text: gāḍhāliṅgana maṅgalaṃ bhavatu te svasty astu vaś cāṭavaḥ
kiṃ brūmaḥ priyayā vilāsakalaha śraddheya evāsi na /
children.translated_text: what shall we say? — of the beloved's playful quarrel are indeed not to be believed.'
'May tight embrace bring you blessing! May you prosper! [But] the flatteries —

children.text: ity ukte nibiḍapravāsacakitair yāvad guṇaiḥ sthīyate
saṃghaṭṭaḥ śivayoḥ sa tāvad adhikaspaṣṭaḥ śivāyāstu vaḥ //
children.translated_text: the collision of the two <s>Śiva</s>s becomes all the more pronounced — may that be for your welfare!
When this is said, while the virtues [of each half] remain standing, startled by the prospect of prolonged separation,

children.text: tad ardhanārīśvaramūrdharatnam
ardhaṃ vidhor astu samṛddhaye vaḥ /
children.translated_text: of that <s>Ardhanārīśvara</s> (Half-Woman Lord), be for your prosperity —
May that half-moon, the crest-jewel

children.text: yad adrikanyāvadanātirikta
dvitīyabhāgabhramam ātanoti //
children.translated_text: creates the illusion of being a second half [moon]!
which, exceeding the face of the mountain's daughter,

children.text: tadvītavyatirekam adritanayādehena miśrībhavan
niṣpratyūham iha vyapohatu vapuḥ sthāṇor abhadrāṇi vaḥ /
children.translated_text: beyond all difference, remove your misfortunes here without obstruction!
May the body of <s>Sthāṇu</s> (Śiva, the Pillar), blending with the body of the mountain's daughter

children.text: veṇyā bhogivadhūśarīrakuṭilaśyāmatviṣā veṣṭitā
jūṭāher api yatra bhāti dayitāmūrtyeva pṛktā tanuḥ //
children.translated_text: even the serpent of the matted locks shines as if joined with the form of the beloved.
[That body] in which, encircled by the braid — dark-hued and sinuous like the body of a serpent-bride —

children.text: prauḍhāḥ kañcukino jaradvṛṣavaraḥ kubjas tuṣāradyutir
nityāpto 'pi bahiṣkṛtaḥ parikaraḥ so 'yaṃ samasto 'py aho /
children.translated_text: an ever-faithful retinue yet banished outside — this entire [retinue], alas!
Mature serpents as body-armor, an aged bull of excellence, a hunchbacked [moon] of snow-white radiance,

children.text: ardhād yadvasatīkṛtād bhagavatā cāritracaryāvidā
sā bhidyād duritaṃ carācaraguror antaḥpuraṃ pārvatī //
children.translated_text: may that <s>Pārvatī</s>, the inner chamber of the Teacher of all moving and unmoving things, destroy [your] sin!
[Yet] from the half made into a dwelling by the Lord who knows the conduct of proper behavior,

children.text: līlodyānavanaśmaśānagamane svecchāparādhīnayoḥ
samyaksāmbaratādigambaradaśāsavrīḍanirvrīḍayoḥ /
children.translated_text: in the states of being fully clothed and sky-clad — one modest, the other unashamed;
In going to the pleasure-garden and the cremation ground — one dependent on another's will, the other on their own;

children.text: paryāptātularāmaṇīyakamahāśrībhairavākārayoḥ
kṣemaṃ vaḥ śivayoḥ samāsamadṛśor diśyād acintyaṃ vapuḥ //
children.translated_text: may the inconceivable body of the two <s>Śiva</s>s, equal and unequal in vision, grant you well-being!
replete with incomparable beauty — one displaying great <s>Śrī</s> (splendor), the other a <s>Bhairava</s> (terrifying) form —

children.text: cūḍendor iva rociṣā mukulitaṃ vātāyanābhaṃ śriyaḥ
pānārthaṃ pariṣevitaṃ madhukarākāraiḥ kumārānanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: attended for drinking by the bee-like faces of [their son] <s>Kumāra</s>,
Closed by the radiance of the crest-moon as if by a lattice-window of beauty,

children.text: aunnatyād adhivāsya vaktrapavanair ghrāṇopayogīkṛtaṃ
kasyorojasarojam asti na manastoṣāya gaurīśayoḥ //
children.translated_text: whose breast-lotus is not a source of mental delight — [that] of <s>Gaurī</s> and <s>Īśa</s> (the Lord)?
brought to service for the nose by the breath of the face due to its elevation —

children.text: ardhaṃ snigdhavimugdham iddhahutabhugdigdhaṃ tathārdhaṃ jagat
pāyād īśvarayos tad akṣi tilakasthānasthitaṃ vīkṣya yat /
children.translated_text: of the two Lords, situated in the place of the <s>tilaka</s> (forehead mark), protect the world — [that eye] seeing which,
Half tender and innocent, half smeared with the blazing sacrificial fire — may that eye

children.text: krīḍākarmaṇi kārmukaṃ karatale kartuṃ kirīṭendunā
sotsekaś ca nirutsukaś ca yugapad devaḥ smaro jāyate //
children.translated_text: the god <s>Smara</s> (Kāma, the Love-god) simultaneously becomes both excessively eager and devoid of eagerness!
in the play of making a bow in the hand with the diadem-moon,

children.text: vyālā vāyubhujas tṛṇeḍhi ca tṛṇāny ukṣā bubhukṣāturo
niṣkaupīnapaṭaḥ kuṭumbabharaṇo kiṃ tv asmi cintākulaḥ /
children.translated_text: [He is] without even a loincloth, yet burdened with maintaining a family — moreover, I am troubled by anxiety!
The serpents are wind-fed; the bull too feeds on grass — yet the bull is tormented by hunger;

children.text: daurgatyād iti piṇḍam ekam akarod gaurīśarūpeṇa yo
yaś cābhīṣṭaphalapradas trijagataḥ kasmaicid asmai namaḥ //
children.translated_text: and who grants the desired fruits to the three worlds — to that certain one, obeisance! (verse)
He who, out of compassion for [their] misery, made one body in the form of <s>Gaurī</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> combined,

children.text: jyāghoṣair badhirīkaroti kakubho bāhū muhuḥ paśyati
svasya svena vikatthate racayati proccaistarāṃ tarjanīm /
children.translated_text: he boasts to himself about himself, he raises his forefinger high in threat —
He deafens the quarters with the twang of his bowstring, he repeatedly looks at his own arms,

children.text: yasmin kevalam eva kelirabhasāj jāte 'rdhanārīśvare
vīraṃmanyatayā sa manmathabhaṭo vātūlitas taṃ stumaḥ //
children.translated_text: that soldier <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love), driven mad by his own bravado — him we praise! (verse)
when merely in the sport of passion the <s>Ardhanārīśvara</s> (Half-Female Lord) came into being,

children.text: vapuḥkhaṇḍe khaṇḍaḥ prativasati śailendraduhituḥ
śikhaṇḍe khaṇḍenduḥ svayam api vibhuḥ khaṇḍaparaśuḥ /
children.translated_text: in his crest, the crescent moon; and the Lord himself bears the broken axe (<s>khaṇḍa-paraśu</s>) —
In one half of his body dwells a portion of the daughter of the mountain-king (<s>Pārvatī</s>);

children.text: tathāpi pratyagraṃ śaraṇam upayātaṃ prati vibhor
akhaṇḍo vyāpāro jagati karuṇāyā vijayate //
children.translated_text: the Lord's undivided activity of compassion triumphs in the world! (verse)
yet toward one who has newly come seeking refuge,

children.text: premnārdhaṃ vapuṣo vilokya militaṃ devyā samaṃ svāmino
maulau yasya niśāpatir nagasutāveṇīniśāmiśritaḥ /
children.translated_text: the moon on his crown, mingled with the braid of the mountain's daughter, night-like —
Seeing that half the body of the Lord has been joined with the Goddess through love,

children.text: āste svāmyanuvartanārtham iva tat kṛtvā vapuḥ khaṇḍitaṃ
deyād advayabhāvanāṃ sa bhagavān devo 'rdhanārīśvaraḥ //
children.translated_text: may that blessed god, <s>Ardhanārīśvara</s>, grant the realization of non-duality (<s>advaya-bhāvanā</s>)! (verse)
[the moon] remains as if having divided its body in order to follow its master;
